editorial:
Imagine living on Earth for thousands of years, watching humanity grow, but never being allowed to step in and help. That is the life of the Eternals, a group of ancient aliens with superpowers who have been hiding in plain sight. When a tragedy strikes, they finally come out of the shadows to fight the Deviants, mankind's oldest enemy. The movie has a huge cast, including big names like Angelina Jolie and Salma Hayek, and it feels like a mix of a superhero story and a family drama. You will see them travel across the world, from ancient Babylon to modern London, trying to figure out who they really are and what their true purpose is.

The action scenes are big and colorful, and the special effects look great on a big screen. The acting is solid, especially from the leads, but with so many characters, some of them do not get enough time to shine. The pacing can feel slow in the middle, and the story tries to do a lot at once. Still, if you enjoy Marvel movies and want something a little different from the usual formula, this one is worth your time.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you learn that the Eternals were actually sent to Earth to prepare it for the birth of a new Celestial, a giant being that would destroy the planet. Sersi stops the Emergence by turning the Celestial into stone using her powers. Then, in a twist, Arishem the Judge takes Sersi, Phastos, and Kingo into space to judge humanity. Meanwhile, Thena, Makkari, and Druig are on their ship when Eros, Thanos's brother, arrives to help them. The movie ends with a cliffhanger, leaving you wondering if the Eternals can save their friends.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Marvel movies and big ensemble casts.
